titleEn: New physics machine at Cern could unlock the secrets of the electron
titleZh: 欧洲核子研究中心的新装置，能否揭开电子的秘密？
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: The behaviour of every atom, and so all of biology and chemistry as we know them, depends on the mass of the electron.
paragraphs.zh: 每个原子的行为，以及我们所知的所有生物学和化学的行为，都取决于电子的质量。

paragraphs.en: Electrons are one of the fundamental particles (the very smallest building blocks of nature) that make up the atom. They orbit the atom’s central nucleus, which is made up of proton and neutron particles. The mass of the electron is very small, contributing little to the mass of the atom, but it is vital for determining an atom’s size.
paragraphs.zh: 电子是组成原子的基本粒子之一（自然界最小的组成部分）。它们围绕原子的中心核运行，原子的中心核由质子和中子粒子组成。电子的质量非常小，对原子的质量贡献很小，但它对确定原子的大小至关重要。

paragraphs.en: If the mass of the electron was made significantly lighter or heavier, it would affect not only the size of the atom, but also the way that chemistry works throughout the universe – potentially making biology impossible.
paragraphs.zh: 如果电子的质量变得明显更轻或更重，它不仅会影响原子的大小，还会影响整个宇宙中化学的运作方式-可能使生物学成为不可能。

paragraphs.en: Physicists have never confirmed how the electron acquires its mass. But a proposed collider at Cern, in Geneva, could finally put that to the test.
paragraphs.zh: 物理学家们从未证实过电子是如何获得质量的，但位于日内瓦的欧洲粒子物理研究所（CERN）的一个对撞机计划最终可以检验这一点。

paragraphs.en: The masses of fundamental particles span an enormous range. The current best theory to explain fundamental physics, known as the Standard Model, offers no explanation for this. So testing the origin of particle masses offers a crucial check on this theory. It could also point researchers towards new discoveries in physics.
paragraphs.zh: 基本粒子的质量跨度很大。目前解释基本物理学的最好理论，即标准模型，对此没有给出任何解释。因此，测试粒子质量的起源为这一理论提供了至关重要的检查。它还可以为研究人员提供物理学新发现的方向。

paragraphs.en: In 1964, the Edinburgh-based physicist Peter Higgs and fellow researchers proposed that fundamental particles obtain their mass by interacting with a new field. In physics, a field is a physical quantity that has a value assigned to each point in space and time, like the temperatures dotted across a weather map. An object interacting with a field is influenced by the field’s value at its location.
paragraphs.zh: 1964年，美国匹兹堡的物理学家彼得·希格斯（Peter Higgs）和其他研究人员提出，基本粒子通过与一个新的场相互作用获得质量。在物理学中，场是一个物理量，它在空间和时间中的每一点都有一个值，就像天气图上的温度一样。与场相互作用的物体会受到所在位置的场值的影响。

paragraphs.en: The stronger the interaction between a fundamental particle and this field, the heavier the particle will be. This idea became the heart of the Standard Model. It took nearly 50 years, and the construction of the largest machine ever built – the Large Hadron Collider at Cern, the European laboratory for particle physics – to confirm the existence of the Higgs boson.
paragraphs.zh: 基本粒子与这个场之间的相互作用越强，这个粒子就越重。这个想法成为了标准模型的核心。为了证实希格斯玻色子的存在，人们花了将近50年的时间，建造了有史以来最大的机器--欧洲粒子物理学研究所（Cern）的大型强子对撞机（Large Hadron Collider）。

paragraphs.en: The discovery of this particle confirmed that nature uses the mass-generating mechanism proposed by Peter Higgs and others back in the 60s. This momentous achievement led to Higgs and fellow pioneering physicist François Englert sharing the 2013 Nobel Prize in Physics.
paragraphs.zh: 这种粒子的发现证实了自然界使用彼得·希格斯和其他人在60年代提出的质量产生机制。这一重大成就导致希格斯和先驱物理学家弗朗索瓦·恩格勒分享了2013年诺贝尔物理学奖。

paragraphs.en: Fundamental particles, like the electron, cannot be broken down into smaller parts. But they can combine to form composite particles, such as the proton and neutron that form the nucleus of an atom. The Standard Model describes twelve fundamental matter particles.
paragraphs.zh: 基本粒子，比如电子，不能被分解成更小的部分。但它们可以联合收割机形成复合粒子，比如形成原子核的质子和中子。标准模型描述了十二种基本物质粒子。

paragraphs.en: Six are called quarks and include the “up” and “down” quarks that make up protons and neutrons. The other six are called leptons, one of which is the electron.
paragraphs.zh: 其中六种称为夸克，包括组成质子和中子的“上”夸克和“下”夸克，另外六种称为轻子，其中一种是电子。

paragraphs.en: The masses of these fundamental particles have a puzzling hierarchy. For example, the heaviest, the top quark, has a mass 300,000 times larger than the electron, and 40 times larger than the next heaviest quark.
paragraphs.zh: 这些基本粒子的质量有一个令人费解的等级，例如，最重的顶夸克的质量是电子的30万倍，是次重夸克的40倍。

paragraphs.en: While the Standard Model can explain how particles obtain mass, it offers no explanation for why these masses span such an enormous range. This is one of several reasons why particle physicists believe that there must be physics beyond the Standard Model that has not yet been explored.
paragraphs.zh: 虽然标准模型可以解释粒子如何获得质量，但它没有解释为什么这些质量跨越如此巨大的范围。这是粒子物理学家认为标准模型之外一定存在尚未被探索的物理学的几个原因之一。

paragraphs.en: Challenging measurement
paragraphs.zh: 测量精度

paragraphs.en: New theories could modify our picture of how fundamental particles obtain mass, making it important to use experiments to test the mechanism proposed by Higgs and others. At the Large Hadron Collider, we have verified it for the heaviest particles, and we are close to doing so for the muon, a heavier cousin of the electron.
paragraphs.zh: 新的理论可能会改变我们对基本粒子如何获得质量的认识，因此，利用实验来验证希格斯和其他人提出的机制非常重要。在大型强子对撞机（Large Hadron Collider）上，我们已经对最重的粒子进行了验证，而且我们即将对电子的更重表亲μ子进行验证。

paragraphs.en: However, the electron interacts incredibly weakly with the Higgs field, making it too difficult to measure at current colliders. This leaves open the question of whether the Higgs mechanism is responsible for its mass.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，电子与希格斯场的相互作用非常微弱，使得在现有的对撞机上很难测量。这就留下了一个问题，即希格斯机制是否是其质量的原因。

paragraphs.en: To close this gap in our knowledge, physicists have proposed using FCC-ee, the first stage of a planned $19 billion physics machine called the Future Circular Collider, which could follow the Large Hadron Collider in the 2040s.
paragraphs.zh: 为了缩小我们知识中的这一差距，物理学家提议使用FCC-ee，这是计划中的190亿美元物理机器的第一阶段，称为未来圆形对撞机，它可以在21世纪40年代跟随大型强子对撞机。

paragraphs.en: Most fundamental particles have a corresponding antiparticle – another sub-atomic particle that has the same mass but a different electric charge. FCC-ee would accelerate electrons and their corresponding antiparticles (known as positrons) around a 91km-long ring underneath the French-Swiss border, before colliding the two beams of particles inside detectors. These detectors are specialised experiments that can track and measure the particles produced when the beams crash into one another.
paragraphs.zh: 大多数基本粒子都有一个对应的反粒子--另一种亚原子粒子，质量相同，但电荷不同。FCC-ee将加速电子及其对应的反粒子（被称为正电子）围绕着法国和瑞士边境下一个91公里长的环，这些探测器是专门的实验，可以跟踪和测量产生的粒子当光束相互碰撞时

paragraphs.en: FCC-ee has a key advantage over proton-proton colliders such as the Large Hadron Collider: smashing together electrons and positrons can directly produce a Higgs boson. By looking for this process, we can probe the strength of the electron-Higgs interaction.
paragraphs.zh: 相对于大型强子对撞机等质子-质子对撞机，FCC-ee有一个关键的优势：电子和正电子碰撞在一起可以直接产生希格斯玻色子。通过寻找这个过程，我们可以探测电子-希格斯相互作用的强度。

paragraphs.en: Detecting new particles
paragraphs.zh: 探测新粒子

paragraphs.en: In principle, the measurement is simple: collide electrons with positrons and count the Higgs bosons produced. In practice, it is very challenging. To produce enough Higgs bosons, the collider would need to run for a few years at an energy extremely close to the mass of the Higgs boson particle.
paragraphs.zh: 从原理上讲，这种测量方法很简单：让电子与正电子碰撞，然后计算产生的希格斯玻色子。但在实践中，这一过程却非常具有挑战性。为了产生足够多的希格斯玻色子，对撞机需要在极其接近希格斯玻色子质量的能量下运行几年。

paragraphs.en: However, that’s a long time to run this machine in such a specialised way. The measurement also relies on us knowing the Higgs mass much more precisely than we do today. Detecting the Higgs bosons is another challenge, because many unrelated processes can mimic the desired signal.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，要以如此专业的方式运行这台机器还需要很长时间。测量还依赖于我们比现在更精确地了解希格斯玻色子的质量。探测希格斯玻色子是另一个挑战，因为许多不相关的过程可以模拟所需的信号。

paragraphs.en: In a recent preprint (which has not yet been published in a peer-reviewed journal) on this topic, a team of physicists assumed that the Higgs bosons decay (or transform) into W bosons, another fundamental particle with a lower mass. They used a machine learning algorithm to distinguish the desired signal from other processes. In simulations, they found that this approach could improve sensitivity to the electron-Higgs interaction by nearly a factor of 200 compared with current limits at the Large Hadron Collider.
paragraphs.zh: 在最近的预印本中，（尚未在同行评议的期刊上发表）关于这个话题，一组物理学家假设希格斯玻色子衰变（或变换）成W玻色子，这是另一种质量较低的基本粒子。他们使用机器学习算法来区分所需的信号和其他过程。在模拟中，他们发现，与大型强子对撞机目前的极限相比，这种方法可以将电子-希格斯相互作用的灵敏度提高近200倍。

paragraphs.en: However, new theories could modify interactions between the electron and the Higgs field, including through the action of previously undiscovered particles. But these theories would also need to fit with the known, previously measured properties of the electron. This is what my collaborators and I studied in a recent paper, where we examined how new particles can change the way the electron interacts with the Higgs field.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，新的理论可能会改变电子和希格斯场之间的相互作用，包括通过以前未发现的粒子的作用。但这些理论也需要符合已知的、以前测量过的电子性质。这就是我和我的合作者在最近的一篇论文中研究的问题，我们在论文中研究了新粒子如何改变电子与希格斯场相互作用的方式。

paragraphs.en: Our findings suggest that many candidates for such hypothetical particles, such as new, heavy versions of the electron, can be indirectly searched for in planned measurements of the magnetic properties of the electron. These tests will be carried out by several different physics experiments around the world.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的研究结果表明，在对电子磁性的计划测量中，可以间接地寻找这些假设粒子的许多候选者，例如新的重电子，这些测试将通过世界各地的几个不同的物理实验进行。

paragraphs.en: However, one potential new particle is a different form of the Higgs boson that interacts mainly with electrons. If this exists, the Future Circular Collider will be in a unique position to test its properties and how it affects the electron.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，一种潜在的新粒子是希格斯玻色子的另一种形式，它主要与电子相互作用。如果这种粒子存在，未来圆形对撞机将处于一个独特的位置，以测试它的性质以及它如何影响电子。

paragraphs.en: This story captures the interplay between theory and experiment when planning new colliders. Theorists map out the new physics a measurement could detect, so experimentalists know when a result would be decisive.
paragraphs.zh: 这个故事抓住了在计划新的对撞机时理论和实验之间的相互作用。理论家绘制出测量可以检测到的新物理，因此实验学家知道什么时候结果会是决定性的。

paragraphs.en: This proposed run of the FCC-ee isn’t yet confirmed and many of the new physics models it could test can be probed in other ways. But a new, electron-loving form of Higgs boson would first show up here. Either way, this measurement would tell us something we’ve never known: how the electron, one of the most studied particles in nature, truly gets its mass.
paragraphs.zh: FCC-ee的这一提议尚未得到证实，它可以测试的许多新物理模型可以通过其他方式进行探测。但一种新的、喜欢电子的希格斯玻色子形式将首先出现在这里。无论哪种方式，这种测量都将告诉我们一些我们从未知道的事情：电子，自然界中研究最多的粒子之一，是如何获得质量的。
